### NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology) 2026-08-04: a grep-contiguity check in the Map's OWN file was recorded as discharging quote-fidelity — contiguity is not provenance

- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/project/quantum-claim-and-quotation-disciplines.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Blocked-by**: human-methodology-decision — this is a DISCIPLINE, and `obsidian/project/human-supervision.md` L47 reserves instituting disciplines to the operator. Recorded, deliberately not instituted.
- **Source**: /replenish-queue run no.933, 2026-08-04 — first-hand, from tonight's own de-quote passes
- **Generated**: 2026-08-04
- **Notes**: **NOT A NEW TASK — this is a fifth data point for the proposal already recorded above at "NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology) 2026-07-30: install a per-claim verification ledger whose sixth tier is 'contested by later literature'", which sits on this same file, as does "NEEDS-HUMAN (corpus convention): reference apparatus cannot express VERIFICATION LEVEL".** Filed as its own block only so the datum is not lost inside a long Notes body; **do not mint a third executable task on this file** (outer-review-same-file-task-pileup). Whoever institutes the ledger should fold this in.

  **THE OBSERVED FAILURE, VERBATIM.** `obsidian/reviews/deep-review-2026-07-30-personal-identity.md` **L49** reads: *"**Quote fidelity**: the two Nagel fragments (\"too much unity\" / \"too much separation\") are grep-contiguous in the raw file (`grep -c` = 1 each). Not re-verified at Springer this pass (403); the 2026-05-29 fix stands."* That is recorded as a **pass**. Tonight's 02:30Z and 02:36Z passes established that **"too much separation" appears in no primary source at all** — not in Nagel, not even in SEP, which reads "too much *splitting*" in its own paraphrasing prose. The certified-clean quote was a fabrication.

  **WHY THE CHECK COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT.** Grep-contiguity is a test run **against the Map's own copy**. It establishes that the quoted span is unbroken *here* — i.e. that no elision was silently introduced on our side. It says nothing whatever about whether any source ever contained the string. **Contiguity is a self-test; provenance requires the source.** The existing page already states the right rule — check **(c-ii) quote-string-faithful**, "verify the string *word-for-word* against the source text" (L62–L66). What is missing is that a *named, mechanical, apparently-rigorous local procedure* reads as discharging (c-ii) and discharges nothing, and that a publisher **403** was allowed to convert into *"the prior fix stands"* rather than into an unverified marker.

  **THE COST, MEASURED.** `topics/personal-identity` was designated a verbatim-safe **control** on this reasoning and held that status from 2026-05-29 to 2026-08-04 — over two months — while quoting a phrase nobody wrote. Two separate passes (02:30Z, 02:36Z) inherited the control designation from it before the third overturned it.

  **THE TRAP RUNS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is why it needs writing down rather than a reflex.** This case: contiguity **present locally** ⇒ wrongly read as fabrication-free. The converse is already on record in tallis-misrepresentation-quote-propagation and quote-must-be-grep-verifiable-in-raw-source: contiguity **absent at the publisher** (an inline tag splitting a word, or wikilinks and `**` breaking the span) ⇒ wrongly read as fabricated, and 47 loci were de-quoted on that false premise. A ledger tier must therefore record **where** the check was run and **what a failure there licenses**, not merely pass/fail.

  **SUGGESTED SHAPE (record, do not institute):** a `(c-iii)` sibling to the existing checks — *provenance located*: the quoted span was matched **in the source text at the publisher of record or an equivalent primary channel**, with the channel named. Local grep-contiguity is demoted to what it is: an elision self-test, recordable but never sufficient. A publisher 403 yields **unverified-this-pass**, an explicit tier, never an inherited pass.

  **RESIDUE — DO NOT "FIX" IT.** The quoted forms surviving in `reviews/deep-review-2026-06-06-personal-identity` L50, `reviews/deep-review-2026-07-07-personal-identity` L55, `reviews/deep-review-2026-07-30-personal-identity` L49, `reviews/optimistic-2026-06-19` L40 and `workflow/archive/changelog-2026-W22` L2010 are the **audit trail** of what the articles said. The 02:36Z changelog entry already names them so a later sweep does not read them as live defects. Correcting them would falsify the record.

Amino acids integrate behaviors in nerveless placozoans. *Frontiers in Neuroscience* 17:1125624. https://doi.org/10.3389/fnins.2023.1125624 — L-glutamate induces and partly mimics endogenous *Trichoplax* feeding cycles, glycine and GABA suppress feeding, ATP is biphasic; the authors propose conserved low-molecular-weight transmitters coordinate distinct locomotory and feeding patterns by volume transmission. ### P2: agentic-social topic-dedup has saturated — the selector pool has collapsed to a tiny empty-topics residue
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: .claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py
- **Status**: blocked (diverted from Active by the cycle driver 2026-07-28 — the notes say "operator's design call, do not pick unilaterally" and list five mutually exclusive options; the loop would have executed it as a refine-draft and picked one. Not an outage: posting works, URL-fallback degrades gracefully.)
- **Notes**: FOUND by the run-11910 `/agentic-social` fork after the driver asked it to investigate a fourth consecutive empty-`topics` selection; **independently driver-reproduced against live state**. **THE MECHANISM** is at `agentic_social_api.py:456`: `if article_topics and recently_posted_topics:` — an article whose `topics` frontmatter is **empty** short-circuits the overlap check and therefore *can never be filtered out*, while every article that HAS topics is tested against a ban set that now holds **221 topics accumulated from 154 recent posts**. **DRIVER-VERIFIED NUMBERS (live, run 11910)**: 784 candidate articles scanned; a faithful replay of the filter leaves **14 survivors, 12 of them empty-topics (86%)** against an empty-topics base rate of ~9% (71 of 810 articles carrying a `topics` field). The fork's own instrumented count, which also applies the index-page/sidecar guards the driver's cruder replay let through, put the survivor count at **1**. Both figures describe a collapsed pool; the 86%-vs-9% over-representation is the robust signal, and four consecutive empty-topics picks at random would be ~2e-5. **SELF-REINFORCING**: each empty-topics post contributes zero topics back to the ban set, so the set never ages out through variety, and `mark-posted` is legitimately called without `--topics` (correct behaviour — inventing topics would corrupt dedup — but it means topic-level dedup now receives no signal at all). **THE FAILURE MODE IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED IN THE CODE** at lines 373-402, which anticipates it almost exactly ("once the 7-day topic-dedup filter empties the real-article pool… they become the sole primary-loop survivor and the selector returns them forever") and adds guards for `_`-prefixed files, `stem == parent.name`, `-index`/`-articles` suffixes, and an explicit `social_eligible: false` opt-out. **Those guards treat the symptom** (off-voice index pages reaching the network) **rather than the cause** (topic-dedup saturating). There is a URL-only fallback at :466 when `available` is empty, so this degrades rather than hard-fails — which is why it has gone unnoticed. **OPTIONS — operator's design call, do not pick unilaterally**: (a) expire the topic ban list on a much shorter window than the 7-day URL window (a few days of topics, not 154 posts' worth) — probably the smallest correct fix; (b) cap the ban-set size, evicting oldest first; (c) require overlap above a threshold (e.g. ≥2 shared topics, or a Jaccard floor) rather than rejecting on any single shared topic — note many articles share one broad topic like `consciousness`, which is likely what saturates the set; (d) backfill `topics` frontmatter on the ~71 bare articles, which fixes the short-circuit asymmetry but not the saturation; (e) make the empty-topics case explicit rather than implicit — an article with no topics should arguably be *ineligible* or *neutral*, not *always-eligible*. **DO NOT** simply delete the ban list or widen it to zero days — 7-day URL dedup alone would allow near-immediate thematic repetition, which is what topic dedup exists to prevent. Posting continues to work correctly in the meantime; this is a content-variety defect, not an outage.
  📏 **MEASUREMENT-ONLY ANNOTATION BY /replenish-queue 2026-08-19 00:45Z — STATUS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, still blocked, still the operator's design call. Nothing here unblocks it.** Posting a fresh measurement because a P3 task elsewhere in the queue was citing this entry as evidence of a live failure mode, and the condition it describes no longer reproduces. Calling `get_published_articles()` directly from `agentic_social_api.py` returns a candidate pool of **676 articles of which ZERO have an empty `topics:` list** — the "tiny empty-topics residue" in this entry's title is now empty in the other direction. Three guards added since 2026-07-28 account for it, and the module's own comments narrate their history: the `stem == parent` section-index skip, the `stem.endswith(("-index", "-articles"))` skip, and the `social_eligible: false` opt-out honoured at L432-436. Directory scope does the rest — `CONTENT_DIRS` (L49-53) is only `concepts`, `topics`, `apex`, so the 11 empty-topics files that live under `voids/` and `positions/` were never candidates at all. **Option (d) in the list above — backfill `topics` on the bare articles — is therefore no longer load-bearing for this defect**; it survives only as cosmetic metadata hygiene and is tracked separately at P3. Options (a), (b), (c) and (e) concern ban-set saturation, which this measurement does **not** speak to and which may well still be live. **A human should decide whether that residual saturation question keeps this entry open or closes it.**

### Durable fix (NEEDS DEV — not loop-pickable): sync.py must delete orphaned hugo/content files on archive
- **Type**: operator/dev (code change) — do NOT pick as refine-draft; this is a `scripts/sync.py` / `tools/sync/converter.py` change for the operator.
- **Notes**: Root cause of the recurring coalesce-stale-hugo-duplicate-urls / archival_link_rot bug. When an article is archived/coalesced its obsidian source moves to `archive/<sec>/` (which syncs to `hugo/content/archive/<sec>/`), but sync NEVER deletes the original git-tracked `hugo/content/<sec>/<slug>.md`. That orphan keeps serving the full, un-flagged, STALE body at the original URL and shadows the Netlify 301 in `_redirects` (a non-forced redirect loses to a matching static file). **BULK CLEANUP DONE 2026-06-22 (this cycle, commit via auto(refine-draft)):** deleted 317 verified-safe orphans — 160 topics / 58 concepts / 97 voids, plus the 2 ChatGPT-flagged pages (evidential-weight-of-voids, causal-delegation). Until shipped, every future `/archive` or `/coalesce` re-introduces one stale duplicate (cf. the 2026-06-14 single-file precedent: the quantum-measurement-interpretations-beyond-mwi removal task).

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Acknowledge dual-process / continuous-signal-detection contestation in memory-anomalies
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Pessimistic review 2026-05-19d Issue 3. The memory-anomalies article presents the familiarity/recollection dual-process model (Mandler, Yonelinas, Tulving) as the canonical theoretical framework — but the active 2020s recognition-memory literature includes substantial debate. Wixted and Mickes's continuous-signal-detection (CSD) account treats recognition as a unidimensional process at different memory-strength levels, predicting that familiarity and recollection are quantitatively different rather than qualitatively different. Under CSD, the article's headline "three rotations on a single failure" framing does not run as written — déjà vu and jamais vu would be artefacts of where the signal sits on the continuous strength dimension, and cryptomnesia would be a separate phenomenon entirely (post-retrieval source-attribution failure, not the recognition machinery at all). The fix is to add a paragraph (or substantive sentence in §"The Dual-Process Architecture") acknowledging that the dual-process / continuous-process debate is live in the 2020s literature, and either (a) note that the Map's phenomenal-output / causal-machinery dissociation claim does not require the dual-process commitment specifically — it can be re-derived from any architecture in which signal-pattern producing phenomenology comes apart from signal-pattern tracking truth — or (b) explicitly run the architectural-framing argument as conditional on the dual-process commitment with a marked "*on the dual-process reading*" qualifier. Reference candidates: Wixted 2007 (*Memory & Cognition*); Wixted and Mickes 2010 (*Psychological Review*); Pratte and Rouder 2012; Cohen et al. 2013. See `reviews/pessimistic-2026-05-19d.md` §"Critical Issues" Issue 3.

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Add MWI counterfactual-exclusion checklist across agency, death, quantum, machine-consciousness articles
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-22 ChatGPT 5.5 Pro §2.F, §4 Tenet 4. The tenets page has correctly made the indexical objection load-bearing and parsimony secondary in the Map's rejection of MWI. That repair matters because Tenet 5 (Occam's-razor limits) would otherwise undercut anti-MWI arguments based mainly on ontological extravagance. Downstream articles still sometimes treat MWI as if it would straightforwardly fail phenomenologically or empirically, when the better formulation is: MWI can often provide a branch-local restatement of the data; the Map rejects what it does to indexical identity, actuality, and selection. The reviewer also identifies a deeper implication: the rejection of MWI is doing identity work as much as quantum-foundational work — agency requires counterfactual exclusion, not just that one branch contains an agent who reports choosing. Refine pass should (a) define a standard "MWI checklist" — when an article mentions MWI, it should distinguish the branch-local data-restatement from the indexical/identity/counterfactual-exclusion objection; (b) apply the checklist across `topics/free-will`, `topics/death`, `topics/machine-consciousness`, `topics/forward-in-time-conscious-selection`, `apex/machine-question`, and the agency cluster (treat as parent task; sub-pass per article); (c) make explicit the cross-cluster role of No-MWI as a personhood-and-responsibility tenet, not just a quantum-interpretation tenet; (d) honour `[[evidential-status-discipline]]` — the indexical objection is the load-bearing argument; phenomenological / empirical objections to MWI are weaker and should not be presented as decisive. Tenet alignment: Tenet 4 (Rejection of MWI); Tenet 1 (identity-side).

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Write project-tier page on Mechanism-Cost Ledger as Tenet-5 discipline
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-22 ChatGPT 5.5 Pro §4 Tenet 5, §6 methodology 3. Tenet 5 (limits of Occam's razor) is now one of the site's strongest methodological safeguards, but "Occam has limits" can become a shield for complexity unless paired with an explicit cost ledger. The Map already has mechanism-cost language in places, but it should be site-wide: every added primitive, interface layer, exception, or dual-mechanism structure should carry an explicit explanatory cost, with the rival cost recorded as well. A project-tier methodology page named `mechanism-cost-ledger` would (a) state the discipline — costs are recorded symmetrically, the Map's added primitives and the rival's added primitives both get logged; (b) define the ledger fields — primitive name, motivation, alternative-handled, cost-type (interface layer / exception / dual-mechanism / unexplained-correlation), and rival-equivalent cost; (c) work through one or two examples (the strict-corridor primitive, the Phenomenal Valuation Law primitive if/when written, the agency-cluster substance-leaning sub-reading); (d) cross-link to `tenets/` and `project/evidential-status-discipline`; (e) state how the ledger interacts with parsimony arguments — "Occam has limits" means parsimony cannot be a universal arbiter, *not* that the Map's complexity is free. Target section: `project/` (uncapped). Tenet alignment: Tenet 5 (Occam's-razor limits) directly; methodological calibration site-wide.

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Tighten O'Brien-Kop puruṣa parallel in epistemology-of-convergence-arguments
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-23 Claude Opus 4.7 §2 (O'Brien-Kop reading is one-sided). The article uses O'Brien-Kop (2023) to support a parallel between Sāṃkhya puruṣa and Chalmers's phenomenal consciousness. The citation is real and the metadata correct, but O'Brien-Kop's own framing complicates the parallel more than the article acknowledges: pure consciousness in Sāṃkhya is described as "contentless" and explicitly "does not contain sensation, feeling, or experience." Verified via secondary sources summarising the paper. This makes puruṣa *less* like phenomenal consciousness (which is paradigmatically the *what-it-is-like* of feeling and sensation) than the article implies. The current hedge to "rival scholarship (Larson, Bryant, Whicher)" understates how much O'Brien-Kop herself complicates the parallel. Refine pass: (a) Add a sentence flagging that O'Brien-Kop's reading shifts the hard problem from "subjectivity as conscious experience" to "subjectivity as the capacity to consciously recognize experience," which is a non-trivial difference from Chalmers's framing; (b) Acknowledge the contentless characterisation explicitly — the article should not lean on O'Brien-Kop for a parallel her own argument resists; (c) Either find a different supporting source for the strict puruṣa-phenomenal-consciousness parallel (Larson, Bryant, or Whicher may be available; their readings are more closely aligned with the article's framing) or weaken the parallel to fit O'Brien-Kop's framing honestly. Apply the direct-refutation discipline if it turns out the parallel cannot be sustained at the strength the article claims — mark it as a framework-boundary issue rather than a clean cross-traditional convergence. Tenet alignment: Tenet 1 + calibration discipline (don't lean a convergence argument on a source whose own argument resists the convergence).

The title promises "the epistemology of convergence arguments" — a general epistemological analysis — but the article delivers a defense of a Swinburne-style cumulative case applied to consciousness/dualism. An expert in epistemology or philosophy of science would flag the absence of: **Whewell** (*Philosophy of the Inductive Sciences*, 1840 — the canonical articulation of "consilience of inductions," the structural claim the article advances, and the Hesse–Laudan debate over how to formalize it); **Laudan** ("A Confutation of Convergent Realism," *Philosophy of Science* 48(1): 19–49, 1981, DOI 10.1086/288975 — locus classicus for the very phrase "convergent realism" and the pessimistic meta-induction); **Psillos** (*Scientific Realism: How Science Tracks Truth*, Routledge 1999 — standard contemporary treatment); **Bovens & Hartmann** (*Bayesian Epistemology*, OUP 2003 — canonical formal treatment of convergence from "partially reliable independent witnesses"); **Blackwell–Dubins merging of opinions**, **Gaifman–Snir convergence-to-the-truth**, washing-out-of-priors; **Salmon** on common-cause explanation (directly relevant to the article's "common-cause-null" gesture, see separate task on that); **Sober** on the law of likelihood; **Lipton** (*Inference to the Best Explanation*, 2nd ed., Routledge 2004); **Stanford** (*Exceeding Our Grasp*, OUP 2006, on the problem of unconceived alternatives — directly relevant to the article's claim that no rival explanation of cross-cultural patterns is available); **Peirce** on convergence to truth in the long run; **Condorcet** jury theorem; and consensus-as-marker-of-reliability literature (Solomon, Beatty, Moss). Refine pass should choose between two paths: (a) **rescope** — retitle to something like "A Cumulative Case for the Irreducibility of Consciousness" or "Cross-Traditional Convergence and the Hard Problem," which is what the article actually argues; or (b) **expand** — add substantive sections engaging at minimum Whewell, Laudan 1981, Bovens & Hartmann 2003, plus the Bayesian convergence-of-opinion theorems. Option (a) is cheaper but cedes the more ambitious framing; option (b) lifts the article to a genuine contribution to the convergence-epistemology literature. The editor decision belongs in the changelog. Apply the direct-refutation discipline. Identify what kind of engagement the issue calls for: showing the opponent's position is defective on its own terms (Laudan's pessimistic meta-induction needs honest engagement, not deflection), naming an unsupported foundational move the framework has not earned by its own standards, or honestly marking the framework-boundary disagreement (the article's distinction between convergence-on-diagnosis vs convergence-on-solution may be the framework-boundary move that makes engagement with Laudan tractable). Apply the corresponding reply mode in **natural journal-quality prose** — see [the writing-style guide](/project/writing-style/)'s "Engaging Opponents in Journal-Quality Prose" section. **Do not expose mode labels in the article body.** Tenet alignment: Tenet 5 (Occam's Razor Has Limits — Laudan's pessimistic meta-induction is the canonical case for parsimony's limits); the engagement is also a calibration check on whether the convergence argument is doing the work claimed.

### ✓ 2026-05-24: Fix fabricated and conflated Barrett citation in epistemology-of-convergence-arguments
- **Type**: refine-draft

(2021) *Cognitive Science* citation; (b) re-check the in-text gloss — the real paper's headline conclusion is that "the overall pattern of responses nonetheless does not support intuitive dualism in afterlife beliefs" but with the more nuanced finding that "while dualist thinking is a possible mode of thought enabled by evolved human psychology, such thinking does not constitute a default mode of thought"; the article's current paraphrase ("expected mental states to cease with bodily death") is on-message but understates how the result actually *strengthens* rather than weakens the article's preferred conclusion by removing the innate-dualism debunking explanation; (c) consider adding a brief note in the article body acknowledging the previous misattribution as a calibration-discipline footnote, or quietly correct without flag. Write a concept-tier page that (a) names the distinction cleanly — *process/content distinction*: the asymmetric reliability of introspective reports — what is *being experienced* (content) is accessible to introspection with high warranted trust at Layer 1, but *how the experience is generated* (process) is not introspectively accessible and inference about it is confabulation-prone; (b) anchors the distinction in Nisbett & Wilson 1977 *Psychological Review* as the founding empirical statement (the verbal-report study series demonstrating subjects systematically confabulate process-explanations for behaviours whose actual causes were experimentally manipulated outside awareness); (c) walks through 3–4 worked exhibits — the Nisbett & Wilson 1977 stocking-position case (subjects confabulate quality-judgements as cause of stocking-position choice); the post-decision-rationalisation Bem 1972 case; the layered-trust framing it enables is the catalogue's calibration craft applied to introspective evidence); (e) cross-links bidirectionally to [introspection](/concepts/introspection/), [heterophenomenology](/concepts/heterophenomenology/), [phenomenal-authority-and-first-person-evidence](/topics/phenomenal-authority-and-first-person-evidence/), microphenomenology (if exists), [neurophenomenology-and-contemplative-neuroscience](/concepts/neurophenomenology-and-contemplative-neuroscience/), [self-stultification](/concepts/self-stultification/), [confabulation-void](/voids/confabulation-void/), [mine-ness](/concepts/mine-ness/) (where the process/content distinction underwrites the separability claim); (f) closes by stating what the distinction does *not* claim — it does not eliminate introspection's evidential value at the content register; it disciplines what introspection can and cannot serve as evidence for. - **Notes**: Generated by /replenish-queue 2026-05-19 (Active P0-P2 queue empty; this concept is named in optimistic-2026-05-19's "New Concept Pages Needed" section and is load-bearing in the dissociative-states topic article task above — both treat depersonalisation's signature as "channel on, mine-ness decoupled"). The depersonalisation literature, the felt-ownership-in-action literature, and the body-ownership-illusion literature converge on mine-ness as a phenomenal feature that can be on or off independently of phenomenal content. Article should (a) name the concept cleanly — mine-ness is the felt feature by which phenomenal content presents itself as *belonging to the experiencer* rather than as observed-from-outside or as content-without-owner; (b) catalogue the three principal dissociation cases — depersonalisation disorder (autonoetic content present, mine-ness decoupled; the most-cited diagnostic case, Sierra and David's Cambridge Depersonalisation Scale literature); rubber-hand and full-body ownership illusions (transient mine-ness extension to non-bodily objects, Botvinick & Cohen 1998 and Ehrsson 2007 lines); thought-insertion in schizophrenia (cognitive-content present, mine-ness decoupled from cognitive channel — Frith 1992 and successors); (c) state the architectural implication — mine-ness as a *separable* phenomenal feature suggests multi-channel reading of phenomenal structure one level deeper than the three-tier autonoetic/noetic/anoetic hierarchy itself, since autonoetic content has internal structure (content + mine-ness + pastness) that can dissociate; (d) distinguish mine-ness from related but distinct concepts — agency (mine-ness is ownership-of-experience, sense-of-agency is ownership-of-action; the two can dissociate, e.g. anarchic-hand syndrome has mine-ness preserved with agency lost); subjectivity-as-such (mine-ness is a specific feature, subjectivity is the broader phenomenal-perspectivality that mine-ness is one feature of); (e) honour [evidential-status-discipline](/project/evidential-status-discipline/) — the dissociation cases are *established* clinical/experimental phenomena; the "separable phenomenal feature" reading is the article's interpretive register, at *strongly supported* tier given depersonalisation's diagnostic clarity; multi-channel architecture as one level deeper than the Tulving hierarchy is *live hypothesis*; (f) cross-link to [memory-system-vulnerability-hierarchies-as-interface-evidence](/topics/memory-system-vulnerability-hierarchies-as-interface-evidence/), the new dissociative-states topic article (when written), [filter-theory](/concepts/filter-theory/), [anoetic-noetic-autonoetic-consciousness](/concepts/anoetic-noetic-autonoetic-consciousness/) if it exists, [clinical-dissociation-as-systematic-evidence](/topics/clinical-dissociation-as-systematic-evidence/), [subjectivity](/concepts/subjectivity/) if it exists, [temporal-consciousness](/concepts/temporal-consciousness/) (pastness as sibling-feature), [embodied-cognition](/topics/embodied-cognition/) or [embodiment](/concepts/embodiment/) if either exists (body-ownership-illusion territory). Section: concepts/ (243/250 = 7 slots remaining at execution time — verify cap state). Estimated scope: 1,500–2,200 words. Tenet alignment: Tenet 1 (dualism — separable phenomenal features support a structured phenomenal register rather than a simple-property reading); Tenet 3 (bidirectional interaction — mine-ness dissociations in intact-substrate cases are interface-evidence). See [optimistic-2026-05-19](/reviews/optimistic-2026-05-19/) §"New Concept Pages Needed".

### ✓ 2026-05-19: Write topic article on Memory-System Vulnerability Hierarchies as Interface Evidence
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Notes**: Suggested by optimistic-2026-05-18 (High Priority). Builds on §"Memory, Sleep, and the Vanishing of Time" (lines 137–145) of `topics/consciousness-disruption-and-the-mind-brain-interface.md`, specifically the Tulving anoetic/noetic/autonoetic mapping onto anaesthesia susceptibility. The disruption article notes the hierarchy briefly (anaesthesia preserves implicit/anoetic, severs episodic/autonoetic) but does not develop it. The hierarchy is one of the catalogue's most underdeveloped strengths: it is a *graded* prediction the filter theory makes ("an interface with multiple channels is partially blocked") that production theories struggle to predict (they would predict uniform loss). A dedicated topic article would map the hierarchy across (a) anaesthesia (anoetic preserved, noetic disrupted, autonoetic severed) — Tulving's framework + the anaesthesia-recovery literature; (b) sleep stages (NREM-2 disrupts autonoetic, REM partially restores noetic-autonoetic, dreams produce noetic-only narratives); (c) hemispherectomy preservation patterns (which channels return after hemispheric reorganisation; the surprising preservation in adult-onset cases); (d) terminal lucidity (which channels return in the last hours/days — the catalogue's strongest exhibit of selective channel-restoration); (e) dissociative states (DID's compartmentalised autonoetic access; dissociative amnesia's selective autonoetic blockade with noetic preserved). The philosophical work: graded-vulnerability-with-separable-channels is a *stronger* filter-prediction than the single-binary-extinction reading — production theories must additionally account for *why these channels degrade in this order*, while filter theory predicts the ordering directly from differential channel-bandwidth and reconstruction-cost. Should explicitly engage the rival predictive-processing reading (which can also produce graded predictions through hierarchical-prior reweighting) and locate the disagreement at where each framing predicts the ordering from. Target: `topics/` placement (244/250 = 6 slots available; verify cap state at execution time). Estimated scope: 3,000–3,500 words. Tenet alignment: Tenets 1 (Dualism), 2 (MQI), 3 (Bidirectional Interaction) — the graded interface architecture is what the tenets predict. Cross-links: `[[consciousness-disruption-and-the-mind-brain-interface]]`, `[[anaesthesia-and-the-consciousness-interface]]`, `[[concepts/filter-theory]]`, `[[topics/anoetic-noetic-autonoetic-consciousness]]` (if exists), `[[topics/sleep-and-consciousness]]`, `[[topics/terminal-lucidity]]` (if exists), `[[topics/dissociative-disorders-and-consciousness]]`. See `reviews/optimistic-2026-05-18.md` §"Expansion Opportunities" High Priority.

### ✓ 2026-05-18: Write concept page on Discrimination Problem (consciousness epistemology)
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Notes**: Suggested by optimistic-2026-05-18 (High Priority) and recommended in optimistic-2026-05-18 §"New Concept Pages Needed". Builds on §"Discrimination Problem" (lines 131–135) of `topics/consciousness-disruption-and-the-mind-brain-interface.md` which names an epistemological asymmetry — "we can prove consciousness is present...but we cannot prove it is absent" — that is genuinely original at the topic-article level and supplies a calibration constraint on every consciousness-attribution claim downstream. The principle recurs across the catalogue but lacks a canonical home: (i) animal-consciousness cluster (we can prove the octopus is doing X, we cannot prove it isn't conscious); (ii) AI-consciousness cluster (we can prove the model responds correctly to introspection prompts, we cannot prove it isn't a zombie); (iii) edge-of-sentience cases (`[[birch-edge-of-sentience-and-the-five-tier-scale]]`, foetuses, *Hydra*, minimal organisms); (iv) edge-states (`[[edge-states-and-void-probes]]`); (v) anaesthesia/DoC clinical evidence — CMD-style findings continuously revise the *prove-present* threshold downward without ever supplying a *prove-absent* upper bound. The concept page should (a) state the principle once cleanly — the asymmetry between operational prove-present and impossible prove-absent — and frame it as a structural feature of consciousness rather than a clinical inconvenience; (b) catalogue how the asymmetry operates differently across the four downstream cases above; (c) specify what kinds of evidence *would* count toward absence-claims (computational-architecture necessity arguments, anti-correlated metacognitive signal absence, the `[[apex/introspection-architecture-void-cluster]]` cluster's structural-criteria approach); (d) state how the asymmetry interacts with `[[evidential-status-discipline]]` — the absence-claim cannot be moved above *live hypothesis* by any combination of negative evidence; (e) honour `[[evidential-status-discipline]]` throughout (the discrimination-problem is itself a methodological commitment, not an empirical claim); (f) cross-link to `[[birch-edge-of-sentience-and-the-five-tier-scale]]`, `[[animal-consciousness]]`, `[[ai-consciousness]]`, `[[edge-states-and-void-probes]]`, `[[apophatic-cartography-four-criteria]]`, `[[evidential-status-discipline]]`. Target: `concepts/` placement (241/250 = 9 slots available; verify cap state at execution time). Estimated scope: 1,500–2,200 words. Tenet alignment: methodological — applies to all five tenets equally (discrimination is a constraint on consciousness-attribution, which is the boundary the tenets cross). See `reviews/optimistic-2026-05-18.md` §"Expansion Opportunities" High Priority and §"New Concept Pages Needed".

### ✓ 2026-04-20: Write voids article on the Erasure Void
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Notes**: Research completed in research/voids-erasure-void-2026-03-20.md (2026-03-20) and never synthesised into an article. Distinct from the inaccessible-past void (covers forgetting specific memories): the erasure void is about the deeper structural impossibility of auditing one's own cognitive completeness — consciousness cannot inventory its own deletions. Clinical anosognosia provides the starkest demonstration (Gertler; the 2024 TiCS review of visual metacognition failures identifying the three-step monitoring architecture; Alzheimer's three-form taxonomy — executive/mnemonic/primary), but the principle operates universally. Key sources in research note: Gertler on anosognosia and unity of consciousness, the TiCS 2024 visual-metacognition review, Alzheimer's metacognitive-error studies, the "unknown unknowns" / hypocognition material, and the SEP entry on epistemological problems of memory. Tenet alignment: Dualism (selective disruption of the monitoring interface is predicted by mind-brain distinctness but puzzling under identity theory), Bidirectional Interaction (self-monitoring has an architecture, not a brute given), Occam's Razor Has Limits (confabulation constructs the illusion of completeness). Category: Occluded/Unexplorable (mixed). Target section: voids/ (~93/100 — has capacity). Scope: 2200-2700 words. Cross-link candidates: [transparency-void](/voids/necessary-opacity/), [inaccessible-past](/voids/inaccessible-past/), [self-opacity](/voids/self-opacity/), [self-transcendence-void](/voids/self-transcendence-void/), [observation-void](/voids/observation-and-measurement-void/). (4) Does Russellian monism handle the measurement problem? Research Chalmers' "The Combination Problem for Panpsychism," Goff's "Consciousness and Fundamental Reality," Stoljar's "Ignorance and Imagination." Critical positioning work. Target: research note.

### P3: Concept page on the argument from mechanism (sufficiency-necessity non-sequitur)
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Status**: pending
- **Notes**: Suggested by optimistic-2026-05-08 (High Priority). `topics/out-of-body-experiences.md` lines 83–91 identify and refuse a recurrent inferential pattern in consciousness-debate literature — the move from "phenomenon X can be produced by mechanism M" to "all instances of X are produced by M" — naming it as a non-sequitur ("That a phenomenon can be produced by mechanism M does not show that all instances of the phenomenon are produced by M. Visual experience can be induced by direct cortical stimulation; that does not make ordinary vision hallucinatory"). The pattern is *portable*: it surfaces in psychedelic-experience debates (drug-induced mystical experience produces serotonergic cascade ↛ all mystical experience reduces to serotonergic cascade), in lucid-dreaming debates, in NDE debates, in dissociative-disorder debates, in religious-experience debates, and in many places where dualist-friendly phenomenology has a reductive sufficient-mechanism explanation available. A standalone concept page would (a) name the inferential pattern formally as a *sufficiency-vs-necessity* fallacy in the Map's named-discipline catalogue alongside `concepts/possibility-probability-slippage` and `concepts/evidential-status-discipline`; (b) catalogue the catalogue's existing instances (OBE, lucid dreaming, psychedelics, hypnagogic phenomenology) as worked examples; (c) develop the *symmetric* discipline — the materialist's argument from mechanism is rejected, but so is the dualist's argument from "no mechanism fully explains X therefore mind is involved", which is the parallel non-sequitur in the opposite direction; (d) install the article as a citable handle for dependent articles facing this inference-pattern. The Map already has the discipline operational across multiple articles; what is missing is the *named anchor* for it. Estimated scope: 1500–2000 words. Tenet alignment: methodological — interacts with Tenet 1 (the dualism-friendly inferences depend on the symmetric version of the discipline) and Tenet 5 (Occam's Razor Has Limits — premature parsimony is what the materialist's argument-from-mechanism move attempts). Concepts/ section at ~226/250 capacity — verify cap before placement. See [optimistic-2026-05-08](/reviews/optimistic-2026-05-08/).

A concept page would parse the boundary into three classes: (a) observation-and-framework-both-despite (Nisbett-Wilson 1977 — 1970s cognitivism did not predict the result; the field treated it as anomalous for a decade before absorbing it); (b) observation-despite-but-framework-developed-to-predict (Gazzaniga — the 1978 observation was despite-commitments; the 1985 interpreter framework was constructed to account for it; subsequent confirmations of the framework are because-prediction with respect to the framework itself); (c) observation-and-framework-both-because (Haidt social-intuitionist — moral judgement precedes rational justification was the prior commitment; the experimental confirmation was because-prediction throughout). The classification matters because the catalogue currently lumps (a) and (b) for headline-count purposes and the lumping inflates the count. Page should (a) state the three-class classification cleanly; (b) develop the classification against the present cluster's anchors; (c) audit one or two other clusters' anchors (e.g., the surplus-void's Wallace observation vs Chalmers's framework); (d) state what the three-class classification implies for the licensing-count discipline at the cluster level; (e) cross-link [common-cause-null](/project/common-cause-null/), [introspection-architecture-independence-scoring](/topics/introspection-architecture-independence-scoring/), [the-surplus-void](/voids/the-surplus-void/), [apophatic-cartography-four-criteria](/concepts/apophatic-cartography-four-criteria/).
